chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: Wild Bill Davis versus Jimmy Smith's voltage regulator
summary: Wild Bill played like a band; Smith's dynamic sound came from an overloaded voltage regulator.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Wild Bill played like a band. Jimmy Smith played more or less... He played with a voltage regulator that gave it a dynamic sound. In other words, he turned up the voltage. But the only thing is, if you played something (?), it's

hazardous on the speaker, because it's overloaded. If the amplifier is constantly overloaded, eventually it will rattle. But I guess he made so much money he doesn't care if it rattles. But that was the secret of his success. They said, 'Look how dynamic he is; look!' It wasn't that. It's just that the voltage regulator is so high, that it just really pops(?) it.
